answer_1.quote: Given a history context sequence that contains k utterances ... the task aims to generate a natural language nonverbal message n = {n1, n2, …} for speaker of the k‑th utterance ...
answer_1.outputs: nonverbal messages (short phrases describing facial expressions, body movements, vocal traits, etc.)

answer_2.quote: We use F1 as well as ROUGE‑1 (measuring the overlap ...) and also report DIST‑1/DIST‑2 scores ...

answer_4.quote: Human Evaluation and Error Analysis: we randomly sample 100 instances ... we ask annotators to rate each NM using the following four binary metrics: (M1) relevance ... (M2) fluency ... (M3) validity ... (M4) factual consistency.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each generated nonverbal message on relevance to the utterance, fluency of the phrase, validity (whether it fits a NM type), and factual consistency with the context.
